new_statements.relation_note: tone: *CV1 (first stem syllable) tonally distinct, as in Lwena; no stress/accent remark for K.12a
new_statements.rule_in_words: Guthrie records Luimbi's principal sound-shifts, which in his Inventory include the 'Tones' line, as broadly those of K.14 Lwena apart from listed consonant reflexes; the Lwena entry reads 'Tones: *CV1 only tonally distinct', i.e. the Proto-Bantu high/low contrast survives on the first stem syllable only. By implication Luimbi is a (reduced) tone language; nothing is said about stress, accent or penultimate length.
new_statements.exceptions: none visible; K.12b Ngangela is in turn 'Similar to K.12a'
new_statements.identity_note: Guthrie's K.12a is Luimbi of Angola by definition of the referential classification (Glottolog luim1238 = K12a); Guthrie had first-hand Luimbi data (his 1948 Classification cites 'LUIMBI (12) aa mazi'). The tonal information is stated on the K.14 Lwena entry and carried to K.12a by Guthrie's 'Broadly similar to K.14, but..' convention, under which only the listed (segmental) shifts differ. | group-level statement: Guthrie's K.12 'Luimbi' [Angola] is Luimbi/Lwimbi [lum] (later K.12a in Guthrie 1971 and Maho 2003/2009); the prosodic remarks are stated for 'the languages of the zone' (Zone K) and single out only Ciokwe (11) and Mbunda (15) for penultimate lengthening; no Luimbi-specific data are cited in the visible text. [name in source: Luimbi (12) [Zone K, Group 10]; pages 52 (group list), 53-54 (characteristics of Zone K)]

sources.note: Luimbi appears only as 'Lu-imbi (86 c)', a vocabulary from Fr. Keeling (p. 799). No Luimbi-specific accent remark. The front-matter transcription convention says only, for Bantu generally: 'The accent or pitch of the voice is indicated by '. This is so normally and frequently on the penultimate syllable that the accent is only employed when an exception to the prevailing rule in Bantu transfers the voice-pitch to the first, last, or other syllable than the penultimate.' -- a pan-Bantu convention, not a statement about Luimbi.
